newsitem.title: USA: Georgia Senate approves notice for hospital deals.
newsitem.headline: Georgia Senate approves notice for hospital deals.

text.p: The Georgia Senate unanimously approved a bill requiring disclosure and public hearings before public hospitals could be sold or leased to for-profit companies, a hospital industry official said Wednesday.
The proposal (HB600) now heads into a conference committee to be reconciled iwth a slightly different version aproved in the Senate earlier this month.

"The enactment of H.B. 600 into law will assure the citizens of Georgia that they will have fair warning and the chance to speak out at a public hearing if a for-profit conglomerate ever tries to take over their local community hospital," said Monty Veazey, president of the Georgia Alliance of Community Hospitals.
The proposal would apply to public hospital takeovers by other non-profit hospitals as well as deals involving for-profit corporations. Thirteen other states have enacted similar laws.
